title: Geopolitical Mining Weekly: Recoverable Material as Strategic Supply
discussion_signal: The post describes a shift from treating mineral security as a mining problem toward recovery, reuse, and recycling of material already in the economy. It links U.S. policy treatment of recoverable minerals to battery-recycling programs and argues that retained materials can become strategic supply. This supports the atlas distinction between substitution potential on paper and usable secondary supply, but does not prove scale, collection, processing, or cost competitiveness.
linked_research_question: How much recoverable material can reach U.S. industrial users at the right purity, timing, and cost to reduce import dependence rather than merely improve a policy narrative?
limits: The post is a research relay and does not measure recovered volumes or delivered substitution
Policy inclusion does not establish industrial-scale recovery
It does not resolve processing, collection, or market-price constraints
